description: A composite, two-row by four-column figure comparing the hierarchical martensitic structure of two experimental steels. Rows are labelled on blue tabs at left as "0Al" (top) and "1.3Al" (bottom); columns are headed by green chevrons reading "Prior austenite grain", "Packets", "Blocks", "Laths". Column (a) is a pair of colour-coded EBSD orientation maps (scale bar 20 μm) showing equiaxed, polygonal prior austenite grains rendered in many discrete colours, with visibly similar grain populations in both steels. Column (b) is a pair of SEM micrographs (scale bar 10 μm) of martensitic packets, each annotated in yellow with bracket-and-line "Packet size" gauges. Column (c) is a pair of colour-coded EBSD maps (scale bar 5 μm) annotated "Block width" in yellow with yellow measurement lines and, in the 1.3Al map, a black arrow; the 1.3Al block map is more finely fragmented in colour than the 0Al one. Column (d) is a pair of TEM micrographs (scale bar 0.2 μm) of parallel, lath-shaped martensite, annotated "Lath width" with yellow line pairs across individual laths. No numeric size values are printed on any panel — only scale bars. Quantification appears only in the caption/citing text. The figure argues that the multilevel martensitic unit sizes are essentially equivalent in the two steels.

observations.observation: The figure is a 2×4 composite: two rows labelled "0Al" (top) and "1.3Al" (bottom), four columns headed "Prior austenite grain", "Packets", "Blocks", "Laths".

Column (a) shows colour-coded EBSD orientation maps of prior austenite grains with 20 μm scale bars; the grains are equiaxed and polygonal, and the 0Al and 1.3Al maps show visually comparable grain populations.
Column (b) shows SEM micrographs with 10 μm scale bars, each annotated in yellow with a bracket-and-line gauge reading "Packet size".
Column (c) shows colour-coded EBSD maps with 5 μm scale bars annotated "Block width" with yellow measurement lines; a black arrow is present in the 1.3Al map.
Column (d) shows TEM micrographs with 0.2 μm scale bars of parallel martensitic laths, annotated "Lath width" with yellow line pairs spanning individual laths.
No numeric size values are printed on any panel of the figure; only scale bars (20 μm, 10 μm, 5 μm, 0.2 μm) and text annotations are legible.
The caption states that (a) is prior austenite grains, (b) martensitic packets, (c) martensitic blocks and (d) martensitic laths in the experimental steels.
The citing text reports average prior austenite grain sizes of 26.1 ± 9.4 μm for the 0Al steel and 23.4 ± 5.9 μm for the 1.3Al steel, described as showing minimal difference.
The citing text states the measurements were performed by EBSD, SEM and TEM on approximately 300 prior austenite grains, 200 martensitic packets, 200 blocks and 100 lath widths.
The citing text states that martensitic packet (dp), block (db) and lath (dl) sizes were comparable between the two steels.
The citing text concludes that martensitic unit size is not the primary factor governing KU₂ and KIC, and suggests a dominant influence from differences in precipitation behaviour.

subfigures.description: Two colour-coded EBSD maps (0Al top, 1.3Al bottom) with 20 μm scale bars, showing equiaxed polygonal prior austenite grains in many discrete orientation colours; grain sizes look comparable between the two rows. No colour key/legend is displayed.
Two SEM micrographs (0Al top, 1.3Al bottom) with 10 μm scale bars, showing martensitic packet/block relief; each image carries a yellow bracket-and-line gauge labelled "Packet size".

Two colour-coded EBSD maps (0Al top, 1.3Al bottom) with 5 μm scale bars, labelled "Block width" with yellow measurement lines; the 1.3Al map additionally carries a black arrow and appears more finely colour-fragmented than the 0Al map. No colour key is shown.

Two TEM micrographs (0Al top, 1.3Al bottom) with 0.2 μm scale bars showing bundles of parallel martensitic laths separated by dark lath boundaries; yellow line pairs labelled "Lath width" measure individual laths.

unreadable_items: No colour key/legend is shown for the EBSD maps in columns (a) and (c), so the individual colours cannot be assigned to specific crystallographic orientations or phases from the pixels alone
No numeric size values are printed on any panel; values in the description come from the caption/citing text, not from the image
The fine detail of the 0.2 μm-scale TEM lath boundaries in column (d) is only coarsely resolved at the supplied image resolution
